correctness.rationale: The anchored-potential representation fixes the articulation vertex, gives a constant-Jacobian map to the zero-sum Euclidean hyperplane, and factors the two complete-clique Lipschitz domains. Permutation symmetry and Dirichlet(1,...,1) order-gap moments give the covariance c_r(I+J) with c_r=(r+2)/(12r). Projecting the independent anchored blocks yields contrast eigenvalues c_a (a−2) and c_b (b−2) and a two-dimensional Gram reduction of trace (ab+a+b)/(6N), determinant (a+2)(b+2)/(144N), yielding the stated radical eigenvalues. Evaluating det(B−c_a I) and det(B−c_b I) negative locates each contrast strictly between λ− and λ+, including zero-dimensional edge classes. For fixed N=a+b−1, the trace-squared/determinant parameter 4(s+N+1)^2/[N(s+2N+6)] increases strictly in s=ab, establishing every balance extremum and κ=N iff equal cliques. Dividing the radical by the enlarging b confirms the finite fixed-a limit. Independently diagonalized projected covariance for (a,b)=(2,2),(2,5),(3,3),(4,7): condition ratios 3, 14/3, 5, about 9.157466; all match the formulas.

value.rationale: A concrete natural graph operation—identifying two complete blocks—produces a nonorthogonal coupling in the intrinsic polar metric. The full covariance eigenspectrum and strict balance extremum answer a motivated shape/conditioning question with exact boundary cases, which cannot be obtained by renaming a known uniform-vertex formula. This is a useful family benchmark for polar graph-polytope geometry; no broader conjecture is required.

limitations: Only two simple unit-weight cliques sharing exactly one vertex, Euclidean intrinsic polar and continuous uniform volume.
Finite eigenvalue tests corroborate analytic proof, not its integer-universal scope.
